title: Cargo Compartments — Replacement of the Lining Panels by Flame Penetration Resistant Items
abstract: Replacement of all cargo compartment lining panels by a phenolic laminate qualified to the revised burnthrough standard, compartment by compartment, on aircraft delivered against the earlier qualification.

sections.planning_reason: A revision to the flame penetration requirement for Class C compartment liners was adopted after this aircraft was certified. The original lining meets the standard in force at type certification but not the revised one, and several authorities have said they will not accept the earlier qualification on aircraft entering their registers after 2022. In-service sampling also shows that panels in the aft compartment lose about fifteen per cent of their burnthrough margin over ten years of loading damage and repair.
sections.description: All lining panels in the forward, aft and bulk compartments are replaced by phenolic laminate panels with a ceramic veil on the fire side. The decor panel D2550136675057 and the restraint lining at the aft bulkhead are replaced together because the joint between them is the weakest point of the assembly. The upper decor panel is attached with anchor nuts EN513769-76 at a revised pitch, and the obsolete curtain rail kit D2550005854497 is deleted where fitted. Panel edges are sealed with an intumescent tape at every joint. The compartment light assembly D2550007254418 is removed for access and refitted unchanged.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Empty the compartment and remove the cargo loading system rollers where they obstruct the lining. Remove the compartment light assemblies D2550007254418 and store them. Remove the lining panels using AMM-T-25-50-11-000-001-A, working from the aft bulkhead forward. Remove the obsolete curtain rail kit D2550005854497 where fitted and blank the fixing holes. Do a general visual inspection of the exposed structure and of the smoke detection sampling line and report any finding. Install the new anchor nuts EN513769-76 at the revised pitch on the compartment ceiling. Install the new lining panels using AMM-T-25-50-11-400-001-A, starting at the aft bulkhead, and fit the decor panel D2550136675057 with it. Apply the intumescent tape at every panel joint and at every penetration. Refit the light assemblies and the loading system rollers. Do the smoke detection sampling performance check for the compartment. Record the embodiment.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable to TITAN-88 aircraft up to and including MSN T00177 that have not been built to the revised liner standard. MSN T00099 is excluded, that aircraft having been withdrawn from service. A compartment must be converted in full; a partly converted compartment does not meet either qualification.
sections.material_note: Kits are supplied per compartment. Kit lead time is thirty weeks and is driven by panel tooling. Removed panels are scrapped locally under the operator's waste procedure and must not be re-used on another aircraft. Intumescent tape has a twelve-month shelf life from the date of manufacture.

type_data.compliance_time: Before the aircraft is entered on a register that applies the revised requirement, or within 96 months after the date of this Service Bulletin, whichever occurs first.
